skills.name: architect
skills.description: Sketch a change's types, signatures, and ownership boundaries before implementing it.
skills.when: Design tradeoffs before implementation
skills.example: Use architect to sketch module boundaries before a refactor.
skills.limits: The active repository owns implementation gates.

skills.name: arena
skills.description: Compare independent candidates under one rubric and combine only compatible improvements.
skills.when: Several independent candidate approaches are useful
skills.example: Use arena to compare two implementations against one rubric.
skills.limits: Candidate writers need isolated paths.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: deslop
skills.description: Remove speculative code and needless structure from a candidate without changing behavior.
skills.when: Candidate contains extra code or abstraction
skills.example: Use deslop after behavior is verified.
skills.limits: Rerun affected behavior checks.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: figure-it-out

skills.example: Use figure-it-out to run the shortest discriminating experiment.
skills.limits: External writes retain their approval gate.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: git-safe-state-auto

skills.name: how

skills.name: interrogate

skills.name: no-comments

skills.limits: Keep comments that explain real invariants.

skills.name: poteto-mode

skills.example: Use poteto-mode to implement a bug fix in verifiable units.

skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-attack-the-premise
skills.description: Apply when repeated fixes sharing an assumption fail. State the assumption and choose an observation that can challenge it before trying another fix that depends on it.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the attack the premise principle
skills.example: Read principle-attack-the-premise while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-boundary-discipline
skills.description: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the boundary discipline principle
skills.example: Read principle-boundary-discipline while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-build-the-lever
skills.description: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the build the lever principle
skills.example: Read principle-build-the-lever while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
skills.description: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction. Encode the rule as a lint, metadata flag, runtime check, or script instead of more text.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the encode lessons in structure principle
skills.example: Read principle-encode-lessons-in-structure while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
skills.description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the exhaust the design space principle
skills.example: Read principle-exhaust-the-design-space while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-experience-first
skills.description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the experience first principle
skills.example: Read principle-experience-first while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-explain-the-number
skills.description: Apply before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the explain the number principle
skills.example: Read principle-explain-the-number while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-fix-root-causes
skills.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom to its root cause and fix it there; reproduce first, ask why until you reach it, resist nil-check guards that silence crashes.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the fix root causes principle
skills.example: Read principle-fix-root-causes while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-foundational-thinking
skills.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the foundational thinking principle
skills.example: Read principle-foundational-thinking while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
skills.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the guard the context window principle
skills.example: Read principle-guard-the-context-window while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-laziness-protocol
skills.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the laziness protocol principle
skills.example: Read principle-laziness-protocol while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
skills.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the make operations idempotent principle
skills.example: Read principle-make-operations-idempotent while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
skills.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the migrate callers then delete legacy apis principle
skills.example: Read principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-minimize-reader-load
skills.description: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace. Count layers between question and answer, and hidden state in the reader's head; collapse one-caller wrappers and shrink mutable scope.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the minimize reader load principle
skills.example: Read principle-minimize-reader-load while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-model-the-domain
skills.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files. Encode the domain in a structure instead of scattered conditionals.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the model the domain principle
skills.example: Read principle-model-the-domain while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
skills.description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work. Proceed, present the result, let the human course-correct after the fact; reserve confirmation for irreversible actions.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the never block on the human principle
skills.example: Read principle-never-block-on-the-human while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
skills.description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the outcome oriented execution principle
skills.example: Read principle-outcome-oriented-execution while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-prove-it-works
skills.description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the prove it works principle
skills.example: Read principle-prove-it-works while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
skills.description: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from day one, instead of bolting it on.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the redesign from first principles principle
skills.example: Read principle-redesign-from-first-principles while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
skills.description: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object. Eliminate the sharing first; serialize structurally only when one shared writer is a real invariant.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the separate before serializing shared state principle
skills.example: Read principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
skills.description: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs. Break work into small units that each end in a verifiable state, check each before the next, and order delivery so the sequence proves itself to a reviewer.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the sequence verifiable units principle
skills.example: Read principle-sequence-verifiable-units while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
skills.description: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite. Remove dead code, redundant validators, and stub references first, then build on the simpler base.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the subtract before you add principle
skills.example: Read principle-subtract-before-you-add while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
skills.description: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Identify a relevant defect and check that the test detects it. Assert the required result or observable effect, including absence when the contract requires it.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the test behavior not implementation principle
skills.example: Read principle-test-behavior-not-implementation while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: principle-type-system-discipline
skills.description: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language. Make illegal states unrepresentable, brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, refuse to lie to the compiler, exhaust variants, derive from authoritative schemas.
skills.when: A decision or review calls for the type system discipline principle
skills.example: Read principle-type-system-discipline while reviewing a relevant change.
skills.limits: Apply only where the task trigger fits; repository rules remain authoritative.
skills.provenance: MIT pstack-derived skill, adapted for the Windows package

skills.name: swarm
